name: Person Mountain Biking
baseMeaning: A picture of a figure on a knobby-tired bicycle, riding over uneven ground. Read in a message it lands as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb.
tldr: 🚵 Person Mountain Biking. In a chat it comes across as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb.

contextMeanings.meaning: The plain reading: a figure on a knobby-tired bicycle, riding over uneven ground. Nothing hidden in the drawing itself.
contextMeanings.example: Planning a weekend off in the hills 🚵

contextMeanings.meaning: Borrowed as a reaction, it reads as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb.

contextMeanings.meaning: In a dating thread the gesture is usually doing the work of a line that was not typed. It arrives as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb, softened by whatever sentence sits next to it.

In a work channel it is read the same way it is read anywhere else — marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb — but the stakes of a misread are higher, because the sender is often talking about somebody's actual work.

platformNotes.note: In Slack 🚵 lands in channels where the sentence was supposed to be shorter. It is usually standing in for planning a weekend off in the hills, and a channel where the topic is somebody's workload is where it misreads.
On Discord 🚵 is a staple of the reaction bar, which is why it so often arrives stripped of its marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb reading — a shape pressed rather than a message sent.

On X and Twitter 🚵 does most of its work in replies, where it tags a message like bragging about a rough downhill run. Short enough to survive being the whole post, which is exactly why it is used that way.

On iOS the Person Mountain Biking 🚵 renders as the neutral drawing, and the neutral swatch is what most people send without thinking about it. A message like planning a weekend off in the hills is the kind that carries it — the picture lands before the sentence does.

WhatsApp renders 🚵 exactly as the phone system does, but the keyboard keeps it in the sport section, where nobody looks unless they are hunting for it. In family threads it tends to accompany a message like bragging about a rough downhill run.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z reaches for 🚵 to do the work of planning a weekend off in the hills, and treats the neutral drawing as the default rather than as a choice. What they hear first is marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb.

Millennials tend to send 🚵 deliberately, usually for something like bragging about a rough downhill run, and they read marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb into it more often than the older cohorts do.
Gen X mostly uses 🚵 literally, as the picture of the gesture itself, and is less likely to read marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb into it than younger senders are.
Older senders use 🚵 in the most straightforward way, on family and group messages, and are less likely to hear the marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb subtext in it.

warnings.title: 🚵 and 🏍️ get swapped
warnings.description: The Motorcycle 🏍️ is one tap away in every picker, and it does not carry the same reading — the motorbike reads speed and traffic, the mountain biker reads rough ground and no engine. Check which one you actually picked.

warnings.title: The reading it usually gets is not the one it was sent with
warnings.description: People take 🚵 as something else fairly often: it gets assumed to mean mountain biking as a sport when it is usually a stand-in for a weekend away from a city, a dusty commute, or an excuse to be outdoors. The sentence around it is usually what settles the meaning.

seoTitle: 🚵 Person Mountain Biking Emoji - What It Actually Means in Text
seoDescription: 🚵 Person Mountain Biking meaning: marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb. How the emoji is used at work, at home and in dating threads, and where it goes wrong.

longForm.overview:
The drawing of 🚵 is a figure on a knobby-tired bicycle, riding over uneven ground. It arrived with Unicode 13.0 in the sport section, and in a conversation it does the work of a line somebody left out on purpose.

The line it stands in for is marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb. That is the reading most people arrive with, and it is usually the intended one — a picture carries the same meaning as the sentence it replaces, and it arrives first.

The complication is that the drawing invites a second reading. It gets assumed to mean mountain biking as a sport when it is usually a stand-in for a weekend away from a city, a dusty commute, or an excuse to be outdoors. In practice that second reading is not rare — it is the one that decides how a message lands, because the sender has usually not thought about it at all.

It also sits in the crowded part of the picker. The nearest neighbour is 🏍️ Motorcycle: the motorbike reads speed and traffic, the mountain biker reads rough ground and no engine. The two are close enough that a fast thumb picks the wrong one, and the message goes out carrying a meaning nobody chose.

The person mountain biking also exists in five skin tones. They are separate pages with separate copy, because picking a tone is a decision in a way that picking the plain emoji is not: it says something about who the sender thinks the reader is.

In short — the person mountain biking reads as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb, it is most often used for planning a weekend off in the hills or bragging about a rough downhill run, and the five tone pages under it each say something different about who is sending it. The rest of the page takes those three apart.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
Context, not the picture, decides how this lands. 🚵 in a work thread is bragging about a rough downhill run; 🚵 in a family thread is planning a weekend off in the hills; 🚵 in a thread with somebody you like is a way of saying something you would rather not type out.

The tone versions of the emoji make the same point from the other side. The gesture is identical in all five, and the swatch says something about the sender before a word is read.

The shortest messages are the risky ones. A lone 🚵 is the whole reply, and it is carrying a meaning nobody wrote down — marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb is the intention, but what arrives is a drawing. Everything the sentence would have disambiguated is simply missing.

Put it this way. Planning a weekend off in the hills is the job the person mountain biking does most: it saves a sentence and lands faster than one would have. Bragging about a rough downhill run is the job it does second: there the picture is not the point, it is the temperature of the message.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Think about what the emoji is replacing. If the sentence under it is doing the real work, 🚵 will get assumed to mean mountain biking as a sport when it is usually a stand-in for a weekend away from a city, a dusty commute, or an excuse to be outdoors instead, and the thread ends up carrying a meaning nobody wrote.

And keep it away from first contact. There is nothing warm in the drawing, and a person mountain biking gesture used to answer other people's messages tends to sound like it is settling a point.

Keep it out of the formal register. In a thread about somebody's work, or in a message to somebody you have not met, 🚵 reads as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb, and formality is exactly where that reading does the most damage.

Leave 🏍️ Motorcycle for the other message. The motorbike reads speed and traffic, the mountain biker reads rough ground and no engine. And keep 🚵 out of threads where somebody is hurting: it reads as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb there, because there is nothing in the drawing that says you meant well.
longForm.howToReply:
The safe move in an unclear thread is to answer the text. 🚵 gets assumed to mean mountain biking as a sport when it is usually a stand-in for a weekend away from a city, a dusty commute, or an excuse to be outdoors often enough that the sentence matters more than the picture.

And do not send 🚵 alone when the message underneath is supposed to be warm. A message like planning a weekend off in the hills carries the feeling; the picture on its own leaves the reader choosing between marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb and something sharper.

Start by reading what the 🚵 was doing. If it was a reaction, react: 🚵 back, and the thread is closed. If it was aimed at you, write. The difference matters, because the reply to a reaction can be a picture and the reply to a request cannot.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🚵 and its skin-tone versions?
faqs.answer: The tone variants under person mountain biking show the same gesture in five different skin tones. The gesture does not change, but the tone is a small signal about who the sender imagines the reader is, and in some groups that signal is read louder than the sentence.

faqs.question: What does 🚵 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 🚵 is used for marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb. The drawing shows a figure on a knobby-tired bicycle, riding over uneven ground, and that part is not in dispute — what changes is whether the sender is being literal or borrowing the gesture for a reaction.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🚵 and 🏍️?
faqs.answer: The motorbike reads speed and traffic, the mountain biker reads rough ground and no engine. The two sit close together in most pickers, so the difference is often about which one the sender pressed rather than about what they meant.

faqs.question: Is 🚵 rude?
faqs.answer: It can be. The gesture is meant as marking trail riding, weekends, or a hard climb, but it gets assumed to mean mountain biking as a sport when it is usually a stand-in for a weekend away from a city, a dusty commute, or an excuse to be outdoors. The risk is highest when it is the only message in the thread — a sentence gives the picture some context to sit in.

faqs.question: What does 🚵 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Nothing gender-specific. The same reading applies whoever sends it, and the meaning is set by the thread and by what is written next to it rather than by the sender.

conversationExamples.interpretation: A public sign-off, with the emoji as the full stop. The picture is doing the punctuation, which is why it is sent instead of a sentence.
